title: Compatible-Section Bed Sharing and Behavioural Risk in a Shared Medical-Tourism Hospital Department: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Discrete-Event Simulation
description:
A behaviour-explicit hybrid agent-based and discrete-event simulation, built in AnyLogic, of a multi-specialty international-patient hospital department that serves medical tourists and local patients from the same beds, specialists and appointment slots.

Patient behaviour is part of the operational logic rather than post-hoc discussion: medication adherence, doctor switching, online versus in-person channel choice, and early abandonment all feed back into flow. Compatible wards borrow each other's idle beds through inter-agent message passing, and the discrete-event layer carries visits, hospitalisation, recovery and re-presentation.

Across 30 randomized-seed replications, compatible-section bed sharing reduces the mean inpatient admission queue by 43 percent (25.9 to 14.8 days, p < 0.001) against an otherwise identical discrete-event-only model. The agent layer also reproduces patient abandonment, emergency escalation and realistic throughput that a pure discrete-event model suppresses by construction.

Requires AnyLogic 8.9.8 (Personal Learning Edition or higher). An interactive web build runs on AnyLogic Cloud without installation.
